title: MCP (Model Context Protocol): how agents reach tools, and where you can stop them
summary: The page needs corrections to the reach of registry blocking: Microsoft now explicitly limits enforcement to governed pathways, not direct access to the underlying service. The advanced connector policy row also labels a single-environment UI route as an environment-group control. The cited pages were accessible in this check; the earlier rate-limit responses did not establish missing documentation.

claims.claim: An administrator blocks a registry MCP server through Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab. ... Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select **Block** to restrict the server across your organization

claims.claim: Individual registry tools are controlled through Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > Enabled / Disabled toggle > Save.
claims.quote: Select the **Tools** tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an **Enabled** or **Disabled** toggle. ... Turn individual tools on or off as needed. ... Select **Save** to apply your changes

claims.claim: MCP server registration requests are approved through Agents > Tools > Requests (preview) > MCP server request > Approve.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Requests (preview)** tab. ... Review the server name, publisher, requester, and request date. ... Select **Approve** to make the server available in the organizational registry

claims.claim: Registry blocking determines whether an MCP server and every tool it exposes are available across the organisation, without qualifying the invocation pathway.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server (including WorkIQ MCP) blocks usage through governed Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) pathways. It doesn't automatically disable the underlying API or service endpoint outside that governed path
claims.fix: Change the row's governs text to 'Whether an MCP server and its tools are available through governed Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 admin center pathways'. Add to its note: 'Blocking does not automatically disable direct access to the underlying API or service endpoint; that requires separate service or API policy.' Make the same changes in the rendered table, using https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers.

claims.claim: Registry tool toggles determine which individual tools are enabled, without limiting enforcement to gateway-mediated experiences.
claims.quote: The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces the policy at runtime for supported tools and experiences that use the gateway. Don't assume the policy applies across all products or connected components.
claims.fix: Change the row's governs text to 'Which individual MCP tools are enabled in supported experiences using the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway'. Add to its note: 'Runtime enforcement applies to supported tools and experiences that use the gateway, not automatically across all products or connected components.' Apply the same qualification to the registry tool-control risk bullet and rendered row, using https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers.
